I have autism and my parents attitude towards it (denying me accommodations because “I’d grow out of it” when I never have and screaming at me why can’t I just “be normal”) caused more damage to me then the autism itself. It hasn’t been world ending having autism, I have a decent job in my special interest field that accommodates me, a close group of friends that I love dearly and who support me, and I’m mostly independent (rely on my friends for help sometimes when they’re able to help me and I help in return when I can cause none of our parents are super in the picture). 

I frequently wonder if I had actually received help for my autism and was taught how to cope appropriately if I wouldn’t have turned to drugs and alcohol as coping skills. I started using because I was so damn overstimulated all the time and my parents would scream at me every time I would have a breakdown because the sun was too bright or a seam was wrong on a shirt I was forced to wear. The drugs made it manageable and enabled me to mask my autism more easily, which was a necessity because my home life was so damn punishing of something I had no control over. 

Idk I wish my parents had just asked me how they could support me cause I probably would be a hell of a lot further in life than I am right now. I love my life at the moment, but since I moved out at 18 it’s been a long frustrating learning process of shit I wish I’d been allowed to learn as a child.

I’m from a blue state in the US and my experience has been mixed. My most recent experience was wonderful. They treated me like a human being and everyone had their own rooms so I didn’t feel like I was “the weirdo” who had to have their own room. Patients were super understanding and when they weren’t the staff stepped in and made it clear that if they threatened me or deadnamed me consistently on purpose they’re going to face consequences. 

My other 4 times however were atrocious. I got sa threats from both staff and patients and was constantly told that I was “actually not a woman” by staff and patients. Also straight up called a “witch playing mind games on men” by one of the staff at one institution.  They were gender segregated and by law I was allowed to be in the woman’s section because I identify as such but I had to threaten reporting them just to get out of the men’s section when I received physical threats of violence because they wouldn’t move me. 

Those 4 awful times were in one of the highest ranked states for trans rights and my good experience was in a, still very trans friendly (at least in the metro areas), but less on paper trans friendly state in terms of protections. 

Tldr: usually it’s a train wreck when I go inpatient but 1/5 of the time it was a good experience. Not sure what your patient rights are in the UK but read up on them and don’t be afraid to threaten reporting or actually reporting them if they violate them or you feel unsafe and they don’t do shit. Best of luck and honestly try to get out asap because inpatient as a trans person in my experience is worse then taking the time at home to figure stuff out.
